Subject: Follow-up & ask: latency/throughput SLOs after today's demo

Hi Marissa / Dev / Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the walkthrough of the Redwood runtime and the dedicated capacity options. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can prepare for the technical workshop: 

Key pain points we surfaced today:
- Tail latency spikes during peak traffic (we see 95th->99th jump from ~120ms to ~460ms)
- Throughput variability when we push concurrent embeddings + generation traffic (spiky CPU/GPU utilization)
- Cost pressure on per-token spend — want to know tradeoffs for quantization & batching
- Need for private deployment options (data residency / compliance)

Primary goals for Q3 pilot:
- P95 latency target: <= 100ms for short form generation (avg request ~150 tokens in/out)
- Sustain 200 requests/sec for synchronous inference workloads during peak windows
- Graceful degradation strategy (fallback to cheaper model or cached responses under load)
- Private deployment in us-west with KMS-managed keys and audit logs

What we'd like from Redwood before the tech workshop:
1) A short technical recap with proposed SLO targets and suggested deployment topology (GPUs, sharding, batching, caching)
2) Expected throughput and latency numbers for the model family we discussed (open-llama-30b / quantized variants)
3) Any constraints on sequence length / KV cache behavior that we should architect around

Happy to share logs and a short week-of-July schedule for the deeper session.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise technical deep-dive recap and our recommended starting configuration for the Q3 pilot. I've attached a one-page SLO proposal and a topology diagram for your infra team to review (attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf, deployment-topology-diagram.png). I also attached a short security questionnaire we can pre-fill ahead of the workshop.

Executive summary / recommendations:
- Target SLOs (pilot):
  - P95 latency: <= 100ms for requests with ~150 tokens total (input + output)
  - P99 latency: <= 350ms with autoscaling and caching enabled
  - Sustained throughput: 200 req/s (concurrent clients), burstable to 350 req/s for short windows
- Model/quantization profile:
  - Primary model: open-llama-30b (fp16 baseline)
  - Recommended production profile: int8 quantized variant (AMX-int8 or similar) for cost/throughput tradeoff
  - Fallback: smaller 7b quantized model for graceful degradation (lower cost, lower latency)
- Deployment topology (recommended starting config):
  - Region: us-west-2 (private VPC peering)
  - Dedicated Redwood nodes: 2 x 80GB GPUs (A100/RTX-class) with model sharding + tensor parallelism; planned autoscale policy to add 1 node at 75% GPU utilization
  - Serving layer: continuous batching with max batch size 64 and soft latency cap of 100ms; client-side concurrency limit=8
  - KV / prefix caching: enable per-customer KV cache for repeated context (expect 20-30% token reduction for prompt-heavy flows)
  - Network: colocate model servers in same AZ as customer egress to minimize cross-AZ latency; TLS + KMS-managed keys per your request
- Expected perf numbers (empirical estimate under this config):
  - open-llama-30b int8: ~1200 tokens/sec per GPU (generation), end-to-end P95 ~80-120ms for 150-token requests when KV cache hits are common
  - With batching and two nodes we estimate sustaining 200 req/s for your workload mix (mix of embeddings + generation) with headroom for short bursts

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling and smart-routing: we recommend a policy that prioritizes p95 latency SLOs; when capacity constrained, route lower-priority requests to the 7b fallback model automatically
- Observability: we'll enable token-level cost traces, per-route latency breakdown, and can export audit logs to your SIEM for compliance
- Limits & caveats: very long sequences (>2k tokens) will increase p99 latency; for those flows we recommend async streaming or batched offline processing

Next steps / proposed schedule:
1) Tech workshop (90 mins) — deep perf runbook + reviewing logs you provide. Suggested slots: Tue 7/14 10:00-11:30 PT or Wed 7/15 14:00-15:30 PT.
2) Share your production request distribution and a sample request log (we can use that to tune batching & cache hit expectations)
3) If acceptable, we'll follow with an SOW + reserved capacity quote (DocuSign link included in attachments)

Attachments included:
- redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (one-pager with SLO table & cost estimate)
- deployment-topology-diagram.png (PNG, 420KB)
- security-questionnaire-FinServe.xlsx (XLSX, 36KB)

If helpful, Dev and Dylan can join the technical workshop to go through kernel/quantization tradeoffs and the KV cache internals.

Cheers,
